author: Gregory Thaumaturgus
occasion: The surviving fragments comment on verses from Jeremiah, especially the warning about hypocrisy and the phrase about the circumcised nations, explaining how non-Israelite peoples could be called circumcised.
argument: Gregory opens by applying Jeremiah's warning about a neighbor who speaks peace while harboring enmity to the hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees, arguing that hypocrisy and hidden deceit are deadly, and that every good or evil done to a brother is done to God. He then turns to the question of how Jeremiah can call Egypt, Edom, Ammon, and Moab 'circumcised' alongside Judah. He argues that Egypt and Edom are called circumcised because they descend from Abraham through Ishmael and Esau, while Ammon and Moab descend from Lot, Abraham's nephew. The final move draws a moral lesson: many peoples have only a pretense of righteousness and traces of God's law, stopping at outward appearance without cutting away evil.

outline.move: The fragment applies Jeremiah's saying about a neighbor speaking peace while hiding enmity to the hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees, and warns that hypocrisy and hidden deceit are deadly, since good or evil done to a brother is done to God.

The author raises the question why Jeremiah calls Egypt, Edom, Ammon, and Moab circumcised along with Judah, and begins tracing their descent from Abraham through Ishmael, who was circumcised and married an Egyptian woman.
The author argues that the circumcised in Egypt and the desert descend from Ishmael, and that Edom descends from Esau, Abraham's grandson, who also received and passed on circumcision.

The author extends the argument to Ammon and Moab as descendants of Lot, concludes that all these peoples are rightly called circumcised, and draws the moral that many peoples have only a pretense of righteousness without cutting away evil.

cast.name: Ishmael
cast.who: Abraham's son by Hagar the Egyptian; ancestor of the circumcised in Egypt and the desert.

cast.name: Isaac
cast.who: Abraham's son by Sarah; father of Esau and Jacob.

cast.name: Esau
cast.who: Isaac's son, father of Edom; received and passed on circumcision.

cast.name: Jacob
cast.who: Isaac's son who did not marry a foreign wife.

cast.name: Edom
cast.who: Esau's firstborn son, ancestor of the Edomites.

cast.name: Lot
cast.who: Abraham's nephew; father of Ammon and Moab through his daughters.

cast.name: Ammon

cast.name: Moab

cast.name: Jeremiah
cast.who: The prophet whose words are being commented on.

cast.name: Hagar
cast.who: Abraham's Egyptian maidservant, mother of Ishmael.

key_terms.sense: Hypocrisy, outward pretense of piety or virtue that conceals inward evil.
Circumcision, the physical sign of the covenant inherited from Abraham, here extended to non-Israelite descendants.
Uncircumcised in heart, meaning inwardly unreformed or still full of evil.
Hidden deceit or treachery lodged in the heart, used to deceive the simple.
Pride or arrogance, linked with empty glory and opposed to acknowledging God as the source of all good.
False glory or empty reputation, the deceptive self-esteem that accompanies pride.
The seed or descendants of Abraham, the genealogical basis for calling various nations circumcised.
A pretense or outward show of righteousness that does not reach the heart.
Evil or wickedness that must be cut away from oneself.
The law of God, including the command to have no other gods, which the nations are warned not to learn from.

scripture: The author uses Septuagint book names and numbering, including Genesis and Jeremiah. Citations should be given in modern form with LXX Psalm numbering where applicable.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Jacob, source_forms: [Ἰακώβ], who: Isaac's son who did not marry a foreign wife.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὁ μέντοι Ἡσαῦ ἠ-γάγετο γυναῖκα τὴν θυγατέρα Ἰσμαὴλ... ὁ μὲν Ἰακὼβ οὐκ ἠγάγετο γυναῖκαν αἵμα-τος ξένου, οὐδὲ τῶν Χαναναίων, ταῦτα ἐπι-σκέψαντος τοῦ πατρός.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Isaac's son who did not marry a foreign wife or a Canaanite, with his father's oversight.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Ammon, source_forms: [Ἀμμών], who: Son of Lot by his younger daughter; ancestor of the Ammonites.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἐτέχθη γὰρ τῇ μὲν πρεσβυτέρᾳ ὁ Μωὰβ... καὶ τῇ δευτέρᾳ Ἀμμὼν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Son of Lot by his younger (second) daughter; ancestor of the Ammonites. Note: Moab was born to the elder daughter, Ammon to the younger/second daughter.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Moab, source_forms: [Μωάβ], who: Son of Lot by his elder daughter; ancestor of the Moabites.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἐτέχθη γὰρ τῇ μὲν πρεσβυτέρᾳ ὁ Μωὰβ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Son of Lot by his elder (first) daughter; ancestor of the Moabites. Note: The source says πρεσβυτέρᾳ (elder/first) for Moab and δευτέρᾳ (second/younger) for Ammon.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Ammon and Moab descend from Lot, Abraham's nephew.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: τοὺς υἱοὺς Λὼτ, τοῦ ἀδελφιδοῦ Ἁβραάμ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Ammon and Moab descend from Lot, Abraham's nephew (ἀδελφιδοῦ, literally 'son of a brother/sister', i.e., nephew or more precisely the son of Abraham's brother Haran).
